title: Locomotion Options UI (Wrist Menu integration)
description:
Purpose: Provide runtime selection and tuning for locomotion modes (teleport, slide head-relative, slide controller-relative) and turning (snap vs. smooth), plus comfort aids, seated/standing calibration, and height offset. Accessible via the Wrist Menu (X). This task exposes a UI page and runtime bindings that enable/disable the corresponding builtin locomotion mechanics.

Controls (Quest 3 mappings — verbatim from BuildSpec):
- X Button: Open wrist menu / mission log / settings panel; Tap to cycle HUD modes if menu is closed. This page appears under Settings > Locomotion.
- Left Thumbstick: moves on ground (when a sliding locomotion is active).
- Right Thumbstick: snap or smooth turns (snap by default; smooth optional).

Runtime bindings expected in params_json (examples read by CMechanicBinding::Entry::params_json):
- enable_teleport (bool): whether builtin.locomotion.teleport is enabled.
- enable_slide_head (bool): whether builtin.locomotion.slide.head_relative is enabled.
- enable_slide_controller (bool): whether builtin.locomotion.slide.controller_relative is enabled.
- turn_mode (string): "snap" | "smooth".
- snap_angle_deg (float): 30/45/60 options.
- smooth_turn_speed_degps (float): 90–240 range.
- vignette_intensity (float): 0.0–1.0, applied on sprint/boost (forwarded to sprint/flight if present).
- height_offset_m (float): -0.3 to +0.3 for seated/standing calibration.

Behaviour, frame-by-frame:
1) On init, registers a Locomotion settings subpage with the HUD/Wrist Menu system (see dependency). Reads saved settings (if available) and reflects them as current toggles/sliders.
2) When the Locomotion page is open, user can:
   - Toggle between Teleport / Slide (Head) / Slide (Controller). At least one must be active; multiple can co-exist but only one sliding profile is active at a time.
   - Choose Turn Mode: Snap or Smooth. If Snap, choose angle (30/45/60). If Smooth, choose speed (deg/s).
   - Adjust Vignette Intensity (0..1). This value is published to other mechanics via a comfort bus (mechanic-local singleton; see Integration).
   - Adjust Height Offset; applied additively to camera rig Y.
3) Applies changes immediately:
   - Enables/disables builtin mechanics by id (teleport/slide.* and snap_turn) via mechanic registry.
   - Applies updated snap angle and cooldown to builtin.locomotion.snap_turn.
   - Publishes smooth turn speed for other systems to read if smooth-turn is implemented elsewhere.
   - Updates a small on-wrist status chip showing the currently active locomotion profile.
4) On menu close, persists settings via the Save/Persistence service.

Components read/write:
- Reads: CMechanicBinding (for params_json), player rig transform (CTransform), input state.
- Writes: a small CUIState for Locomotion page, a CComfortState for vignette/turn preferences, CPlayerSettings for height offset.

Comfort/safety:
- Never applies camera roll; height offset clamps to [-0.3, +0.3] m; changes lerped to avoid pops.

Acceptance hooks:
- On first load in central_battery_plaza, posts a Wrist Menu hint toast "Open Wrist Menu (X) to choose your locomotion" (satisfies test_entry_point_spawn prompt to open locomotion menu).
- During test_locomotion_menu_modes, changing toggles immediately enables the corresponding builtin mechanics and the turn style.

Integration points and depends_on:
- Depends on hud_and_wrist_menu (id: hud_and_wrist_menu) to register a Settings > Locomotion page with controls and to show the initial hint toast.
- Exposes a small ComfortBus within this module (publish-only): { vignette_intensity, turn_mode, snap_angle_deg, smooth_turn_speed_degps } that other generated mechanics (e.g., ground_sprint_overlay, flight_system) may read via a shared ECS singleton component tag CComfortState.
- Activates/deactivates builtins by id: builtin.locomotion.teleport, builtin.locomotion.slide.head_relative, builtin.locomotion.slide.controller_relative, builtin.locomotion.snap_turn.

Assets and scenes:
- UI uses ring_hud_ui_pack for sliders/toggles styling.
- Active in all scenes; initial hint is only fired in central_battery_plaza.

Suggested file split: locomotion_options_ui_register.cpp (page registration + settings), locomotion_options_ui_runtime.cpp (apply settings, publish comfort), locomotion_options_ui_toast.cpp (first-time hint).
